From powertrain plant to engine campus: SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 for Indianapolis NDT technicians

An Indianapolis NDT career rarely stays under one certification scheme. The metro builds transmissions, makes diesel engines just south in Columbus, runs large pharmaceutical plants, and builds aircraft engines too: Rolls-Royce, which employs more than 3,500 people at its Indianapolis site, makes and tests defense engines there, including the F130 ordered by the Air Force in 2021 to re-engine the B-52, and in 2026 completed a decade-long modernization of the campus with new engine test cells. The airport adds aircraft maintenance on top. Follow one technician through three jobs and the difference between ASNT SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 becomes practical.

Stage one: shafts, gears and plant welds

The technician starts in magnetic particle on shafts and gears at a powertrain supplier, then adds ultrasonic weld work for a contractor serving pharmaceutical and utility plants. Automotive customers set their own quality demands, but personnel certification in plants like these commonly rests on an employer written practice built on SNT-TC-1A, and ASME work on vessels and piping calls for SNT-TC-1A directly. Certification comes from the employer, and it ends when the job does. The habit worth forming here is keeping records that will mean something to a later employer: course outlines with hours, an experience log signed off and divided by method and part type, and every examination result.

Stage two: an engine-parts supplier makes an offer

Engine makers and defense primes commonly name NAS 410, or EN 4179, in the quality clauses of their purchase orders, and the clause flows down to every supplier that tests the hardware. On defense work this is long-standing practice, because NAS 410 replaced MIL-STD-410. So an offer from a supplier making engine parts will usually mean certification to a NAS 410 written practice signed off by the company's designated Responsible Level 3 (RL3).

The RL3 reviews the technician's file and decides what to credit. Years of magnetic particle on powertrain parts count as experience, yet the SNT-TC-1A certificate does not meet a NAS 410 requirement by itself, and formal surface-method training is where the file usually falls short, because NAS 410 demands a larger block of it, in penetrant and magnetic particle especially, than SNT-TC-1A recommends. The specific examination then tests the supplier's own procedures and its customers' specifications. A file split by part type helps here: an RL3 can credit forging and machined-part work more readily than a lump total of hours. Brush up with magnetic particle testing training and check the SNT-TC-1A eligibility rules that shaped the earlier certifications.

Stage three: a hangar at the airport

FedEx said in 2023 that it would move heavy maintenance from its Los Angeles hangar to its Indianapolis hub when that lease ended in 2024. Airline and repair-station maintenance runs on a different logic again. The FAA certifies no NDT personnel itself. Under Advisory Circular 65-31B, NAS 410, ATA Specification 105, SNT-TC-1A and three international standards are all acceptable, and each operator or Part 145 repair station picks whichever one its own manual and its customers' contracts specify. Eddy current and visual inspection of structure dominate, with penetrant on parts. Ask which document the manual names before assuming. See eddy current testing in aviation and aviation NDT training for the methods.

For Indianapolis employers that run both programs

A supplier that ships to an engine customer and also does industrial work should keep the two written practices distinct, make each certification letter say which document and revision it was issued under, and update its NAS 410 program to Revision 6, issued in December 2025, when its customers ask for it. Nadcap AC7114 auditors and customer source inspectors start from a signed report and work backward through the inspector's training, experience, examinations and eyesight records. For that audit trail Atlantis provides NAS 410 audit documentation support, drafting and checking the files your RL3 signs off, and aerospace NDT consulting on the SNT-TC-1A side.

Where Atlantis fits

Atlantis sits on the SNT-TC-1A side of that career path and on the records side of both. Our training mixes self-paced online theory, direct access to our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT) for questions, and practice in the Practical NDT simulator; the hands-on skills and the practical examination are completed with your employer, at its facility and to its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Indianapolis. Powertrain plants, contractors and engine-parts suppliers use our Level III consulting for written practices built on SNT-TC-1A and matched to customer flow-down and Nadcap AC7114, for procedures and Level I and II examinations, and for an outside agency Level III. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to central Indiana engine suppliers. Ask the supplier's RL3 whether outside coursework would count toward a NAS 410 certification there before you enroll anywhere. The NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A guide compares both documents line by line.
